### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**16** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **51** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4894cfe16f9a82007b547cf4c83609a801ab2774` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c1580179a5cf7b7ffc2c675effde76d8e86db750` — the merge of head `9f07d719c82b38211cd630e18e26f6f4624d9d01` into base `4894cfe16f9a82007b547cf4c83609a801ab2774`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c1580179a5cf7b7ffc2c675effde76d8e86db750 && git checkout c1580179a5cf7b7ffc2c675effde76d8e86db750
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4894cfe16f9a82007b547cf4c83609a801ab2774 9f07d719c82b38211cd630e18e26f6f4624d9d01 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4894cfe16f9a82007b547cf4c83609a801ab2774 && git merge --no-ff 9f07d719c82b38211cd630e18e26f6f4624d9d01

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4894cfe16f9a82007b547cf4c83609a801ab2774
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f89f99cd0a4f32c2f50b59027df4c3763d582289`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cli/src/utils/installed-plugins-boot.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/one-shot-settings.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/one-shot-crypto-installed-plugins.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/installed-plugin-loader.ts, packages/runtime/src/installed-plugin-loader.test.ts + packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts (the `registerInstalledPlugins` call site, `refuseRefusedInstalledCryptoProviderPlugins`, `refuseTwoCryptoProviderPlugins`, `cryptoProviderPlugins`, `createHostCryptoProvider`), packages/cli/src/commands/secret/rewrap.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/secret/orphans.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/data-migration-plugins.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/plugin-trust-read.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/plugin-install.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migrate.ts (`extraPlugins` registration), packages/core/src/kernel.ts (`use`, `hasPlugin`), packages/core/src/plugin-loader.ts (`loadPlugin`, `verifyPluginSignature`), packages/core/src/security/plugin-artifact-verdict.ts, packages/runtime/src/index.ts; the changeset read as a prose face. Read only: the diff against `main` at the merge base `a61ddc93a`, the blobs via `git show`, PR #31449 as the landed sibling, the head's check-runs.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set, by invocation.** `os secret rewrap`, `os secret orphans` (`oneShotSettingsPlugins`) and the data migrations' settings and storage arms (`data-migration-plugins.ts`, both arms rethrow a `HostCryptoProviderRefusal`) all reach `oneShotCrypto` → `readDeclaredCryptoProvider`. On this head each of them now also reads the installed set, and refuses when (a) a refused installed plugin is not ruled out by `refuseRefusedInstalledCryptoProviderPlugins` (the same codes and `declaredServices` reading as `os serve`, the loader's own failure as `loader_failed` included), (b) config and installed plugins together hold two declarations (`refuseTwoCryptoProviderPlugins` over the combined list), (c) an installed plugin's name is one a host-config plugin takes (`plugin_name_taken`) or cannot be read (`kernel_refused`), judged by the same function. Unchanged: no installations file for this project and environment (`loadHostInstalledPlugins` answers `null`, `readInstalledPlugins` answers `[]`); installed plugins that load and declare nothing, or whose refusal is ruled out (`runtime_undeclared`, `runtime_not_dispatched`, an imported plugin declaring other services), and a disabled plugin (never a refusal, in the loader before the kept artifact is read); no host config at all (installed plugins are still read, as `serve` reads them, and with none declaring the local provider over the existing key stands). A host config that does not read is still refused first, before any installed plugin is read.
- **Same verdict through the same functions.** The read is `loadHostInstalledPlugins`, split out of `registerInstalledPlugins` byte-for-byte (same loader input, same trusted-keys read, same `AppPlugin` wrap, same host-package anchor, same `loader_failed` catch); `registerInstalledPlugins` calls it and is otherwise unchanged. The judgments are `serve`'s exported functions, not copies. One rule IS copied: the name-taken check (`serve` asks `kernel.hasPlugin`, which grows with every `kernel.use`; the one-shot builds a `Set` of the host config's names once and never adds an accepted installed name to it). That copy diverges — see ④ M1.
- **Public surface.** `LoadInstalledPluginsInput.leaveUninstallsPending?: boolean` on `@objectstack/runtime` (exported from the root with `InstalledPluginsLoad`, now also imported by the cli boot helper). Optional, additive, default unchanged: set, the uninstall-pending records are skipped (neither `finishUninstall` nor load, nothing in `removed`/`refused`); unset, the loop is `main`'s. The runtime test pins both arms. Widening arm, declared as such beside the narrowing.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` × 2 (`@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/runtime`) under ruling A on #25105: `Metadata-protocol: none` on both carriers, so the level follows the kind, `patch`, and the BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition are kept. `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset, same wording, with the widening (`leaveUninstallsPending`) named beside it as the closed pair allows; title and changeset carry `!`. ADR-0087 marker present once in the changeset body: `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, the landed analogue of ⑧B (#31449); the PR reports `check:adr-0087-registration` reading `[BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing]`. The banner names who moves (a deployment running the three one-shot commands with an installed plugin `os serve` would refuse, or with two declarations), Before / Now / Who moves and the fix are all present and agree with the code as read, except for the divergences under ④.
- **Disclosure.** PR body (both languages), commit message, changeset, the new docblocks, the test file header and case names: every line describes behaviour in the PR body's own product words (which plugins refuse the run, which are ruled out, what is registered or removed). The why line is the maintainer's fixed sentence. The one consequence-shaped sentence in the diff's reach ("never falls back to the local key, under which nothing that deployment sealed opens") is `main`'s own module header (#31007), untouched. No breach found.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Private plan items 1–3: implemented as planned (the loader input; the read through `serve`'s path, never `kernel.use`; refused → `serve`'s rule; loaded → composed for the two-provider check and the pick; name taken → `plugin_name_taken`). The integration through `os secret orphans` with a signed installed provider was "if the budget allows" and is listed under Not measured — that gap is where ④ M2 sits.
- Named residual (an installed plugin whose name a plugin `os serve` auto-registers takes is refused by `serve` as `plugin_name_taken` and not compared by the one-shot): confirmed on the tree, since the one-shot composes none of those plugins. Park with ⑧C, as offered; the private notes carry what the one-shot does with such a plugin instead.
- `refuseTwoCryptoProviderPlugins` in `serve` still reads `[...stackMountedPlugins, ...resolverMounted]`, so the one-shot now counts config + installed where `serve` does not name a second installed declaration before init. Both still fail on such a composition (`serve` at the kernel's second `registerService`); the one-shot is the stricter of the two. Parked with ⑧C (series item B), no change asked here.
- A pending uninstall: `serve` may produce `uninstall_failed` / `record_changed` and refuse; the one-shot never finishes one, so it never produces those codes and goes on. Accepted: in both the pending plugin is not loaded and is not the provider; the one-shot's own run removes nothing, and the next `serve` boot finishes the uninstall exactly as before. Not a finding.
- Open question answered: the read's side effects on the one-shot process are the same as `serve`'s boot has — a read-only database boot for the trusted keys (`readTrustedKeys`, shut down before it answers, only when a signed install names a key), the host-package resolve hook, and the top-level code of every verified installed plugin (not only the declaring one) running in the one-shot process. Nothing is written: no uninstall finished, no state file touched.

### ④ Design judgment

- **M1 (must-fix) — two installed plugins with one plugin name are not judged as `os serve` judges them.** `readInstalledPlugins` fills `taken` from the host config's names only and never adds an accepted installed name, while `serve`'s `registerInstalledPlugins` asks `kernel.hasPlugin(name)` after each `kernel.use`, so the second installed plugin with the same name is refused `plugin_name_taken` there (carrying its `declaredServices`) and accepted here. `cryptoProviderPlugins` then keeps the LATER of two same-named entries. Consequences: both declare the provider → `serve` refuses the boot, the one-shot runs with the later one; the first declares and the second does not → `serve` seals with the first, the one-shot reads "none declared". The PR's claim that a name clash is refused "as `os serve` refuses them" does not hold for this shape, and the one-shot and `serve` reach different verdicts. Fix: add each accepted installed name to `taken` (one line after the check), plus a test row (two installed, one name).
- **M2 (must-fix) — a SIGNED installed plugin that declares the provider does not boot in the one-shot run.** `oneShotCrypto` composes `declared.plugin` through `refusingNamedOnFailure`, a `Proxy`. The runtime loader records the artifact verdict for a signed install against the plugin OBJECT (`recordPluginArtifactVerdict`, a `WeakMap` keyed by identity, and it sets `plugin.signature`). The kernel's `loadPlugin` reads `signature` through the proxy, then `pluginArtifactVerdict(proxy)` misses, and `kernel.use` throws "carries a signature that no host verified against its artifact". So for the production shape — an installed, signed provider plugin — every one-shot run stops at `bootSchemaStack` with the kernel's message (`boot_failed`), not with the PR's refusal and not sealing with that provider. Fail-closed, but the accept case the PR declares ("an installed plugin that loads and declares the provider is the one the run seals with") is not reached for a signed install, and the operator is told their signature is unverified. The new test file uses unsigned stub plugins and the signed end-to-end is listed as not measured, so nothing pins it. Fix: do not re-wrap an installed plugin (name the failure another way), or record the verdict for the wrapper too (`recordPluginArtifactVerdict(proxy, pluginArtifactVerdict(plugin))`, both exported by `@objectstack/core`'s security index), and add a signed stub (`signature` set, verdict recorded) to the test.
- **S1 (should-fix) — refusal text names the wrong place.** `oneShotCrypto`'s "registered none in this run" refusal and `refusingNamedOnFailure`'s "could not boot" refusal both say the plugin "declares the crypto provider ... in the host config"; for an installed plugin that is false and sends the operator to the wrong file. Say where it was declared (host config or `os plugin install`).
- **Nit.** The one-shot's `kernel_refused` for an unreadable name omits the thrown reason that `serve`'s carries. `oneShotCrypto({ cwd, env })` reads the host config from `cwd` but the installed set from `process.cwd()` / `process.env` (the real callers pass neither, so test-only). The `--database-url` flag of `rewrap` / `orphans` is not handed to the trusted-keys read, which uses `OS_DATABASE_URL` or the project database as `serve` and `os plugin install` do — consistent with the sibling, noted only.
- Held as claimed: the loader change (verified against `verifyInstalledPlugins`'s order — directory check, pending status, disable-state, disabled, kept artifact — a pending record with an unexpected directory is still refused by both); `leaveUninstallsPending` changes nothing `serve` later does; the `loader_failed` shape and `isExitSignal` rethrow; the per-code remedy text reaching the one-shot unchanged from ⑧B (`ownStep` for the five codes, `os plugin disable` otherwise); no host config → installed read; disabled → not a refusal; `tree_changed` → refused, named with code and step; the changeset's Before / Now / Who moves against the code except as M1 and M2 state.
- Check-runs on `f89f99cd0a` at the last poll: every completed run is success or skipped (Build Core, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Type Check workspace / source gates / debt ledger, Lint ESLint and the scoped lints, Test Core 5/8 and 7/8, Live E2E UI, Dogfood gate); still in progress: Test Core 1,2,3,4,6,8 of 8, Type Check consumer gates, Lint repo & tooling / docs & code guards / CI, release & engine gates. No failure recorded.
